en: Cold tiles. My head is pounding. The name inside my coat collar reads ELIAS. It's all I have.
Every clock says 23:59. Nothing moves. Everything holds its breath at the edge of the minute.
The train doors are sealed. From the outside.
A pocket watch, right beside me. The crystal is cracked, but the brass is still warm.
I woke on the arrival platform of Elysium-09. Every clock reads 23:59. A warm, cracked pocket watch lay beside me.
Someone else passed through the West Turnstile seconds before the station froze at 23:59.
Good, you picked up. Stay on the line, Elias. It won't hold for long.
Elysium-09 is under a containment lock. Nothing in here moves past 23:59 unless you move it.
That watch can't turn back the whole station. Only the pieces that broke when it stopped.
Feels like the whole place is holding its breath at the edge of the minute, doesn't it?
Restore auxiliary power in Signal Control. That unseals the street exit. Go through Maintenance.
The man on Call Box 09 knows how my watch works. He sounds tired, and somehow familiar.
Station Bulletin: Emergency Evacuation

ELYSIUM-09 STATION CONTROL // ISSUED 23:54
All passengers must leave the station now.
Exit by the street stairs in the Atrium.
Do not wait for transit service to resume.
ELYSIUM civic stabilization works in progress.
Thank you for your patience.
Station Control ordered an evacuation at 23:54, five minutes before every clock stopped.
Maintenance Clipboard: Shift Log

Day 1: Grid meters ran backward for 4 seconds.
Day 2: Again. Calling it chronometric backflow.
Day 3: Shutter gear slipped twice. Reported.
Day 4: ELYSIUM directors say ignore the meters.
'Expected field behavior.'
I'm logging it anyway.
A technician logged 'chronometric backflow' days before the incident. ELYSIUM's directors said to ignore it.
Security Booth Log and Transit Pass

BOOTH LOG // SECURITY CROSSING // NIGHT
23:50 Gate set to pressure-plate interlock.
23:54 Evacuation bulletin received.
23:56 Two passengers waved through to Lounge.
23:58 Atrium not answering. Holding post.
Transit pass SC-09 clipped to this page.
The booth guard waved two passengers through to the Waiting Lounge at 23:56.
Don't stare at it too long. An echo only does what you already chose to do.
Personal Recorder: Mira

[Static. A woman's voice, close to the mic.]
Elias, if the stabilization fails, don't come
back for me. Promise me you'll let the clock
pass midnight.
[A long breath. Footsteps. The tape ends.]
Memory: The Bench by the Window

Two shapes on the bench, minutes before 23:59.
Mira, holding my sleeve too tightly.
Me, checking the clock again and again.
She asked me to promise.
I don't remember if I did.
That's me on the bench beside her. Mira. I know her name, but I can't hold on to her face.
Mira begged me not to come back for her if the stabilization failed, and to let the clock pass midnight.
Elysium-09 isn't blocked by rubble. An artificial temporal boundary surrounds it, anchored to the Atrium.
Power's back. I can hear the relays from here.
Listen to me. The vestibule door is open. Go straight up to the street exit.
Don't waste time on the dispatch logs in the Atrium. There's nothing up there you need.
The Operator wants me to skip the Atrium dispatch logs. What doesn't he want me to see?
ELYSIUM Threshold Index: Sector 09

Every threshold in this sector is an index node.
Doorways link by index, not by adjacency.
In a field fault, nodes may pair wrongly.
Re-route at the junction relays.
Scratched below: since 23:59 the north arch
keeps opening onto the west one.
Doorways here link by index, not by position. Since 23:59 some of them open onto the wrong place.
Central Dispatch Recorder

CONTAINMENT PROTOCOL: EXECUTED
TIME: 23:59:00   SITE: ELYSIUM-09
STATION SEAL: ACTIVE
AUTHORIZED BY: ELIAS
CLEARANCE: LEVEL-0 ELYSIUM
INPUT: THIS TERMINAL, PALM VERIFIED

DIAGNOSTIC // ACCESS LOG
23:59:00 - USER: ELIAS
23:59:00 - USER: ELIAS
23:59:00 - USER: ELIAS
23:59:00 - USER: ELIAS
23:59:00 - USER: ELIAS
It knows my hand. The seal opened the moment I touched it.
Authorized by Elias. Level-0 clearance. The lock that froze this station came from me.
I sealed Elysium-09 at 23:59. Why would I do that?
And that corner log... the same line, over and over. 23:59:00. Me.
The 23:59 containment lock was executed from the Atrium terminal with my own Level-0 clearance. I sealed the station.
The terminal's access log repeats one line: 23:59:00, USER: ELIAS. A clock fault, or something else?
Now you see why I told you to leave the terminal alone.
Keep moving. She's in the Central District, and the city remembers what you lost.
23:59. The display isn't broken. It just won't change.
Target is no longer present.
An echo cannot claim permanent items or records.
The pocket watch cannot affect this object.
Object is locked in time. Unfreeze it first.
No earlier temporal state recorded for this object.
Already open.
No power to this mechanism.
Route conflict. Clear the active loop on the paired junction first.
Safety interlock: cannot sever the main entry route.
The turnstile rotor is crushed shut. Physical force won't budge it.
Only Rewind can restore this fractured mechanism.
Solid station concrete. No temporal fracture to manipulate.
The counterweight gear is frozen. Unfreeze it before rewinding the shutter.
The shutter is too heavy to freeze directly. Target the counterweight gear.
Too heavy to lift by hand.
The stripped gear has no spring memory. Rewind the fire shutter itself.
Chrono-shielded pressure plate. It only responds to physical weight.
Locked by the floor pressure switch on the south deck.
Chrono-shielded security gate. It cannot be frozen or rewound.
Main power bus is dead. Stabilize the central surge capacitor first.
Breaker is already engaged.
High-voltage insulated switch. The pocket watch cannot affect it directly.
Bulkhead sealed. Synchronize both substation breakers to restore power.
Can't re-engage the West Loop while the North Archway leads to the Atrium.
Route conflict. Uncouple the West Loop at the west junction lever first.
Spatial index relays are anchored outside local time. Switch them by hand.
